qualification: Offline-verified bounded GEM recovery candidate. The observed physical descriptor state and physical recovery are not yet verified.

trigger_evidence.origin: User-provided V2.4 Quick collector and serial logs, request 784
trigger_evidence.previous_physical_result: FAIL: saturation Full timed out with 77 response bytes missing
trigger_evidence.observed_state: offset=602112 total=602112 unsent=0 unacked=77 ref=2 nrtx=0 rtime=4..116 tcp_ticks=67..179 wnd=cwnd=65535
trigger_evidence.confirmed_software_mechanism: Shipped lwIP tcp_rexmit_rto_prepare rejects unacked segments whose first pbuf ref is not 1. This prevents RTO progress despite advancing timers.
trigger_evidence.unknown: No physical GEM BD/register snapshot exists for that V2.4 stall. Missing TX start versus completed-but-unreclaimed ownership remains unresolved.

changes: Every 100ms, native foreground network poll services the GEM TX ring before the TCP timer.
Use the vendor completion reclaimer under SYS_ARCH saved/restored IRQ protection; never force pbuf refs or descriptor ownership.
For remaining head USED=0, TXEN=1 and TXGO=0, issue dsb then STARTTX without resetting TXEN, queue base, descriptors or TCP.
Rate-limited GEM_TX_RECOVERY reports pre-recovery HW/free counts, descriptor status, TXSR/NWCTRL and kick decision outside the critical section.
Vitis explicitly compiles the new source. Collector and Windows freeze select the matching V2.5 manifest.
Retain ACK drain, monotonic TCP timers, 32KiB receive window, batch payload verification, -O2, live GUI binding and removal of the unmeasured Top-1 card.

held_dma_reference.tcp_implementation: Shipped lwIP 2.2.0 core, real pbuf refs, tcp_tmr, tcp_write, tcp_output and RTO logic
held_dma_reference.fault: Hardware boundary retains an extra pbuf reference after output returns ERR_OK; timers advance but RTO remains blocked at ref=2.
assertions: nrtx=0 and tcp_rexmit_rto_prepare=ERR_VAL while the reference is held
No forced reference release for in-flight DMA, no kick while TXGO is active or TXEN is disabled
Completed descriptors release the modeled driver reference; pending idle work receives a guarded STARTTX
Payload bytes match, ref returns to 1, real TCP RTO then retransmits successfully
IRQ state is restored, empty/wrong-adapter/null paths are safe, tight polls do not exceed the cadence
Recovery serial diagnostic renders the descriptor snapshot and kick decision
held_dma_reference.red_green: With an inert recovery function, the same harness failed at the missing-kick and unreleased-reference assertions. With production recovery, all 12 cases pass.
held_dma_reference.limits: GEM MMIO, IRQ state, descriptor completion and vendor reclaimer boundary are modeled. Physical DMA and the vendor reclaimer are not executed on a board in this regression; multi-descriptor chains and ring wrap are not modeled.

tests.retained_regressions: PASS: real-lwIP 100-frame temporary-tail-pressure integration at -O0/-O2, lost1044-byte RTO recovery, fake-boundary ACK drain/sequence wrap, live GUI headless browser, unmeasured accuracy DOM removal, current release packaging/identity binding.
tests.review: Independent read-only source review: no Critical/Important issues; confirmed actual BSP IRQ save/restore and vendor completion semantics. Minor limitation: modeled reclaimer uses one descriptor.

build.identity_checks: Canonical/source/ELF/BOOT checks pass through release-input/package validation. AArch64 disassembly confirms e06_network_poll calls e07_gem_tx_poll before platform_poll_network_timer.
build.warnings: Vendor BSP/FSBL compiler warnings are retained in the log; no warning-free BSP claim.

unverified: Physical GEM state during the observed 77-byte stall and physical effectiveness of STARTTX recovery.
